name: Union of Concerned Scientists: climate, transport and western states (charityevals)
beneficiaries_note: Our build: shares of the result at the defaults. The public money the Inflation Reduction Act won for US households (18.5%) is in the United States; the tonnes (81.5%) spare people everywhere, spread by world population, the small US power-plant and vehicle smoke share left in the world figure.
summary: The Union of Concerned Scientists' climate and clean energy, clean transportation and western states programmes ($32.8M with overhead in the year to September 2025) do technical analysis and advocacy for US climate policy; this model counts the five largest policies it worked on that were won in October 2021 to September 2025 with published tonnes (the Inflation Reduction Act, EPA's 2024 vehicle and power-plant standards, California's Advanced Clean Cars II rule and its 2025 extension of its carbon market to 2045), with its other state clean-energy laws and its climate-accountability science as a share. At the defaults that is 0.0015 years of healthy life per $1,000: a dollar given averts about 0.0056 tonnes of CO₂e (about $180 a tonne), and the public money the Inflation Reduction Act won for US households' home rebates and credits, valued as the recipients' gain less the taxpayers' cost, adds about 3%; the act gives about half of the result; it is low because each win is shared with many groups and with what governments would have done anyway (UCS is credited with 1% to 10% of the advocacy behind each), and the federal rules and the law's credits have since been repealed or cut back and California's car rule has lost its federal waiver. The biggest uncertainties are the discount rate, the shared years a won reform counts and the deaths per tonne; every branch is discounted for missing data, since no tonne is measured for its work.

sections.title: Reach
sections.explainer: Tonnes a year each win of the period would avert once in effect, from the regulators' and modellers' estimates.

sections.title: Effect per unit

sections.title: Adjustments
sections.explainer: For each win: what would have happened anyway, UCS's share of the work, and how much of the win is delivered; then the evidence and missing-data steps, the other wins and the side effect.

sections.title: Air pollution these tonnes carry
sections.explainer: Every tonne avoids its heat deaths; a tonne from burning less fossil fuel near people also avoids air-pollution deaths. These rows say how much of the shared rates applies to UCS's tonnes (docs/normalization.md 2.5).

sections.title: Other outcomes, in tonnes
sections.explainer: The public money won for US households (units of value) is counted in its own unit and enters the tonnes only through the site's fixed bridge (docs/normalization.md 2.6).

sections.title: Outcome
sections.explainer: Tonnes of CO₂e averted per year of the period, per dollar of a typical year's cost.

sections.title: Your dollar's share
sections.explainer: Staff who earn less than they could elsewhere pay part of the cost in kind; and the next dollar does less than the period's average.

rows.label: Evidence adjustment: how far the regulators' and modellers' tonnes should be trusted
rows.explainer: The tonnes are ex-ante estimates by the regulators (EPA, the California Air Resources Board) and modellers (REPEAT), not measured cuts; regulators' estimates of a rule's cuts are sometimes too high (compliance short of the rule) and projections of tax credits have run ahead of what was built. 0.8 (0.5 to 1.1), our judgment, as the Environmental Defense Fund's model for the same kinds of estimate.

rows.label: Inflation Reduction Act's home rebates and credits: UCS's share of the advocacy behind them, relative to its share behind the whole law

The tonnes keep the whole law's share: the home provisions are about 2% of them.

rows.label: Other wins of the period not modelled, as a share of the modelled value
rows.explainer: The five branches are UCS's largest climate wins of the period with published tonnes; the rest of the work, each a share of the modelled value: Maine's 100% clean-power law, Massachusetts' energy law, California's transmission and regional-grid laws, the Midwest grid operator's $22 billion transmission plan and the PJM grid's battery storage, where UCS was one of several advocates (annual report pp. 8-9), 10%; fossil-fuel accountability science (attribution research used in the lawsuits of ten states and in the 2025 International Court of Justice and Inter-American Court opinions, pp. 10-11), whose effect on emissions is far off and uncertain, 5%. 15% (5% to 40%), our judgment.

source.title: Union of Concerned Scientists, 2025 Annual Report (fiscal year 1 October 2024 to 30 September 2025)

rows.label: Side effect: slower nuclear power from UCS's safety campaigns, as a share of modelled value
rows.explainer: UCS's nuclear power safety work (inside the climate programme) presses for stricter safety rules and has opposed some new reactor designs and licence extensions; where that slows or closes a reactor, gas and coal fill part of the gap. Since 2018 UCS has also backed policies to keep safe, economic plants running, which cuts the other way. -2% (-10% to 0), our judgment: small beside the clean-power and vehicle wins, and no closure is attributed to it in the period.

rows.label: Public money won for households, in tonnes of CO₂e
rows.formula: ira_transfer_uov_per_year / (($deaths_per_tco2e * $climate_heat_share * ((1 - methane_share) * (1 + $discount_rate) ^ -$climate_heat_death_delay + methane_share * @climate.methane_heat_deaths_vs_co2 * (1 + $discount_rate) ^ -@climate.methane_heat_death_delay) * (1 + @climate.nondeath_damages_vs_deaths) * (@death_ages.heat_share_under5 * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_under5 + @death_ages.heat_share_5_14 * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_age_5_14 + @death_ages.heat_share_15_49 * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_age_15_49 + @death_ages.heat_share_50plus * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_age_50_74) + ($deaths_per_tco2e * (1 - $climate_heat_share) * air_pollution_weight + extra_deaths_per_tco2e + methane_share * @climate.ozone_deaths_per_tco2e_methane / (1 + ln(1 + $discount_rate) * @climate.methane_lifetime_years)) * (@death_ages.air_pollution_share_under5 * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_under5 + @death_ages.air_pollution_share_5_14 * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_age_5_14 + @death_ages.air_pollution_share_15_49 * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_age_15_49 + @death_ages.air_pollution_share_50plus * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_age_50_74)) * $life_value_multiplier)
rows.explainer: The households' gain enters the tonnes only through the site's fixed bridge (docs/normalization.md 2.6): it moves with the value of consumption, not with the climate sliders.
